focus: So Min-ho May 14-25 release/re-arrest chain: provenance-separated corroboration and public-reaction layer

material_findings.finding: NIHK constitutional-history synthesis cites National Assembly Secretariat, 12th regular session stenographic record No.57 (1952-05-14) for the Assembly action; US FRUS document 135 independently states the Assembly acted May 14 under Constitution Article 49. This is cross-provenance corroboration of the parliamentary act, while the stenographic record itself remains the preferred Korean primary original.

NIHK's preserved Chosun Ilbo report states that So Min-ho was physically released on May 19, left prison at about 20:00, stopped at the National Assembly secretariat, and returned home. The physical release therefore remains distinct from the May 14 Assembly resolution.

A separate contemporaneous Minju Sinbo item preserved by NIHK records an estimated 4,500-person rally in Busan on May 19 attacking the Assembly's So Min-ho release decision and using slogans calling him a murderer. This is evidence of organized public/political pressure around the release, not evidence that the slogans' factual accusations were judicial findings.

NIHK's FRUS-derived Korean database records that martial law was proclaimed effective at midnight May 24/25 for Busan, South Gyeongsang and parts of the Jeolla provinces, and identifies the immediately preceding appointments of Yi Pom Suk as Home Minister, Hong Pom-hui as vice minister, and Yun U-gyeong as police chief. These appointments should be modeled as institutional context rather than automatically as proof of authorship for later arrests.

The release-resolution controversy, the May 19 rally, physical release, martial-law proclamation, and May 25 re-arrest are analytically separate events. Collapsing them into a single 'Busan Political Crisis' node obscures which institution acted, when, and under what claimed authority.

adversarial_checks: May 14 parliamentary action was not silently equated with May 19 physical release.
Rally slogans calling So Min-ho a murderer were preserved as political speech, not converted into adjudicated fact.
Minister/police appointments immediately before martial law were not treated as proof that those officeholders personally authored each arrest order.
The existence of Article 49 authority in FRUS was not used as a substitute for opening the Korean constitutional text and Record No.57.
Secondary accounts of judge An Yun-chul were not promoted beyond the primary-evidence ceiling established in pass269.
The public-pressure layer was separated from the judicial/custodial release layer.
Martial-law proclamation was separated from the subsequent operational re-arrest chain.
NIHK synthesis citations were distinguished from underlying originals.
Contemporaneous press was treated as observation with provenance, not omniscient narration.
No claim was made that the May 19 rally was spontaneous or government-directed without organizer/command evidence.
